# scrollsheet: full documentation text

> Bottom sheets for React that feel native. One primitive for bottom sheets, drawers, modal
> dialogs, side panels, and toasts, built on <dialog> and CSS scroll-snap. Zero dependencies,
> ~<!--size:index.gzip:0-->16<!--/size--> kB gzipped, React 18+, MIT licensed.

This file contains the full text of https://scrollsheet.dev/docs, for models and tools that
can't crawl a live site. The canonical, always-current version lives at that URL.

====================================================================
DOCS - https://scrollsheet.dev/docs
====================================================================

## Install

    bun add scrollsheet

npm, pnpm and yarn work the same way. No peer dependencies beyond React and React DOM, 18 or newer.
ESM only, no CommonJS build.

    import { Sheet } from 'scrollsheet';
    import 'scrollsheet/styles.css';

Entry points: scrollsheet (CSS-external: import scrollsheet/styles.css, plus scrollsheet/toast.css
for toasts), scrollsheet/auto (the same exports with the stylesheets embedded and injected on
first open; use it for no-bundler-CSS setups, Shadow DOM, and CSP with nonce), and
scrollsheet/motion (experimental React-free spring, WAAPI, and scroll-tween core). Never mix the
default entry and /auto in one app. Sheet.* is client-only: in Next.js App Router, add 'use client'
to the file that renders it.

## Styling

    .sheet {
      background: white;
      border-radius: 16px 16px 0 0;
      box-shadow: 0 -8px 40px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.16);
    }

scrollsheet ships mechanics only (position, transform, scroll-snap, backdrop, focus
containment), in scrollsheet/styles.css, which you import once per app. The className on
Sheet.Content lands on the panel, so style it like any card. No bundler CSS handling, Shadow DOM,
or a strict CSP? Import from scrollsheet/auto instead: the stylesheet is embedded and injected on
first open, and nonce on Sheet.Root covers CSP.

Sheets render light everywhere by default, whatever the OS scheme. Set data-scrollsheet-theme="dark"
on an ancestor (usually <html>) to force dark, or "system" to track prefers-color-scheme. Your own
--scrollsheet-bg, --scrollsheet-fg, --scrollsheet-handle and similar variables win in every mode.

## Tailwind

    <Sheet.Content className="bg-white shadow-2xl dark:bg-zinc-900">
      <Sheet.Handle className="bg-zinc-300 dark:bg-zinc-600" />
    </Sheet.Content>

Utilities apply directly, no plugin and no config. Works with Tailwind v4 out of the box. Set
the library's own variables with arbitrary properties, e.g.
className="[--scrollsheet-radius:24px]". State attributes live on the <dialog> ancestor, so
match them with v4's in-* variant, e.g. in-data-[scrollsheet-at-max]:rounded-none. The
mechanics stylesheet only wins where it must (position, transform); everything visual sits in
zero-specificity :where() rules, so a Tailwind utility always overrides it.

## Detents

    type DetentSpec = 'full' | 'medium' | 'content' | number | `${number}px`;

    <Sheet.Root
      detents={[0.35, 0.7, 'full']}
      activeDetent={active}
      onActiveDetentChange={setActive}
    />

A detent is a resting height, resolved to a scroll-snap stop. 'content' measures natural
height, 'medium' is 50% of viewport, 'full' is viewport minus a top inset, and any other number
is a fraction, or pixels above 1. List detents shortest first: the Handle's click cycle, arrow
keys, and slider value follow the order of your array. onTravel(px, progress, info) fires every
frame the sheet moves, also published as --scrollsheet-progress. info.range is [0, tallest detent]
in px and info.progressAtDetents maps each resolved detent height to its 0-1 progress; info is
mutated in place every frame, so read it synchronously.

## Imperative control

    const actionsRef = useRef<SheetActions>(null);

    <Sheet.Root actionsRef={actionsRef} detents={['content', 'full']}>
      {/* ... */}
    </Sheet.Root>

    <button onClick={() => actionsRef.current?.snapTo('full')}>Expand</button>

For the cases a controlled open/activeDetent prop is awkward for (deep links, push
notifications, a descendant reaching up without prop-drilling): actionsRef.current.open(),
.close(), and .snapTo(detent) animate exactly like a controlled prop change would, they're thin
wrappers over the same state. snapTo warns once in dev if detent isn't in the sheet's
configured detents, and still resolves to the nearest one rather than no-op'ing.

## Keyboard

    <Sheet.Content className="sheet">
      <input placeholder="Card number" />
      {/* stays clear of the on-screen keyboard automatically */}
    </Sheet.Content>

iOS resizes visualViewport, not the layout viewport, when the keyboard opens; scrollsheet
listens to it and writes the inset to --scrollsheet-keyboard. The panel overdraws about 120vh
past its bottom edge so a stale frame never shows a gap. No prop, no setup: any sheet with a
text input already avoids the keyboard.

keyboardExpands on Sheet.Root promotes a sheet resting at a short peek detent to the tallest
detent the moment the keyboard actually appears (a measured nonzero inset, never focus alone,
so a desktop click into an input expands nothing) and restores the peek detent when it closes,
unless a drag or controlled change moved the sheet in between. Default false.

Top, left, and right sheets are pinned to their edge, so the panel never moves for the
keyboard; the same inset instead becomes bottom clearance on [data-scrollsheet-body] plus
scroll-padding on the panel, so a focused field near the bottom of a side drawer scrolls clear.

## Desktop drag

    button, a, input, textarea, select, label, [contenteditable], [data-scrollsheet-no-drag]

pointerType: 'mouse' can grab the panel anywhere and drag it; the last ~100ms of pointer
samples project velocity on release, so a flick lands past the cursor. Touch and pen skip this
path and keep riding native scroll-snap. The elements above opt out automatically, add
data-scrollsheet-no-drag to anything else that needs the same treatment.

## Nested and morph

    <Sheet.Root>
      <Sheet.Trigger>Open</Sheet.Trigger>
      <Sheet.Content className="sheet">
        {/* a Sheet.Root rendered in here just works */}
        <Sheet.Root>
          <Sheet.Trigger>Open child</Sheet.Trigger>
          <Sheet.Content className="sheet">Child sheet</Sheet.Content>
        </Sheet.Root>
      </Sheet.Content>
    </Sheet.Root>

Nesting is automatic: a Sheet.Root rendered inside another sheet's content registers with the
parent, which recedes and dims while the child is open, no config needed. Height morphs the
same way, the sheet springs to fit new content whenever it changes inside an open sheet. For a
cross-fade between views instead of a resize, wrap the state update in
document.startViewTransition (feature-detected, falls back to an instant swap).

## Scrollable content inside a sheet

    <Sheet.Content>
      <div data-scrollsheet-nested-scroll style={{ overflowY: 'auto', maxHeight: 300 }}>
        {/* a long list */}
      </div>
    </Sheet.Content>

Mark an inner scroller with data-scrollsheet-nested-scroll and the classic conflict resolves
itself: swiping scrolls the list, and once the list hits its top, the same swipe continues as
sheet travel. Works under handleOnly and disableDrag too; the handoff only widens the drag
surface while a touch that started inside the marked element is live. Any number of elements can
carry the attribute, including ones added or removed while the sheet is open.

The marked element gets the panel's own overlay scrollbar treatment too, controlled by the same
scrollbar prop on Sheet.Root: 'overlay' (the default) hides the native scrollbar and shows a thin
auto-hiding thumb, 'hidden' hides it with no thumb, 'native' leaves it alone. Scrollsheet sets
position: relative on the marked element (under 'overlay' only) to anchor that thumb; overriding it back to static
breaks the thumb.

Not supported inside shadow roots (scroll does not compose across the boundary).

## Side panels

    <Sheet.Root side="right" detents={['340px']}>
      <Sheet.Trigger>Notifications</Sheet.Trigger>
      <Sheet.Content className="sheet">{/* ... */}</Sheet.Content>
    </Sheet.Root>

side anchors the sheet to 'bottom' (the default), 'top', 'left', or 'right'. Left and right
sheets scroll on the x axis instead of y, so detents are widths, not heights. The handle's
arrow-key axis flips to Left/Right for horizontal sides automatically, and the panel's
border-radius/shadow default rounds the lead edge (the one opposite the anchored side).

## Centered dialog and responsive profiles

    <Sheet.Root side="center">
    <Sheet.Root side="bottom" desktopSide="center" desktopBreakpoint={1024}>

side="center" renders a content-sized modal in the middle of the viewport: zoom+fade instead of
travel, no detents, no drag. Your CSS owns the width; core only guards it with
--scrollsheet-center-max-inline (default min(560px, 100%)), --scrollsheet-center-max-block, and
--scrollsheet-center-gutter (default 20px). desktopSide takes the same five values as side and
replaces the presentation once the viewport reaches desktopBreakpoint (default 768, only
meaningful paired with desktopSide). It resolves after mount through matchMedia, so server render
and first paint use side, and crossing the breakpoint while open re-presents instantly.

## Non-modal

    <Sheet.Root modal={false}>

modal={false} keeps the page behind fully interactive: no backdrop, no focus trap, no
inert-ing the rest of the page. It renders on a <div popover="manual"> (top layer,
non-blocking) where the Popover API is available, falling back to a non-modal <dialog>
(.show()) otherwise. Good for a mini player, a map overlay, or a toast, anywhere the page
underneath should keep working while the sheet is up.

## Toasts

    import { Toaster, toast } from 'scrollsheet';
    import 'scrollsheet/toast.css';

    <Toaster />;
    toast('Saved to your list');
    toast.success('Synced', { description: 'Two seconds ago.' });
    toast('Archived', { action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: restore } });

toast() and <Toaster> are part of the package, on their own per-toast DOM (no Sheet.Root
involved): a persistent card per toast, all six positions with per-toast override, stacking that
hides overflow instead of evicting it, and 2-axis swipe-to-dismiss. toast.promise(), useToasts(),
classNames, and per-type icons are included. Toaster props: id, position, visibleToasts (3),
duration (4000), closeButton, expand, gap (14), offset (24), swipeDirections, toastOptions, icons,
hotkey (['altKey', 'KeyT']), containerAriaLabel, nonce, className, style, and sonnerCompat (true).
Style with .scrollsheet-toast classes and --scrollsheet-toast-* custom properties.

## Page transitions

    <div data-scrollsheet-background>{/* your page content */}</div>

    <Sheet.Root backgroundEffect="scale" detents={['full']}>

Mark your page wrapper data-scrollsheet-background, then backgroundEffect="scale" scales,
insets, and rounds it in sync with the sheet's own travel, an iOS-style card transition. Paired
with a 'full' detent, a sheet becomes a full-screen page that pushes the page behind it back
like a stack. 'parallax' shifts the wrapper instead of scaling it. Read
--scrollsheet-stack-progress on a parent sheet's own panel for the equivalent effect between
nested sheets.

## Migrate from vaul

    - import { Drawer } from 'vaul';
    + import { Drawer } from 'scrollsheet';

scrollsheet's vaul compat layer is a drop-in: the same Drawer.* namespace, translated onto
Sheet.*. snapPoints, activeSnapPoint, direction (all four edges), modal={false},
shouldScaleBackground (your [data-vaul-drawer-wrapper] is picked up automatically),
onAnimationEnd, onClose, fadeFromIndex, handleOnly, closeThreshold, snapToSequentialPoint,
onRelease, preventCycle on Drawer.Handle, and asChild all map to real features; nesting needs
no separate NestedRoot. closeThreshold is converted between conventions (vaul counts the drag
away, scrollsheet counts what remains), so vaul's 0.25 default keeps its quarter-height-drag feel when
snapPoints is unset, not scrollsheet's own 0.5.

data-vaul-drawer, data-vaul-drawer-direction, and data-vaul-snap-points still land on
Drawer.Content, and data-vaul-handle on Drawer.Handle, so CSS written against vaul's selectors
keeps matching. Drawer.Title, Drawer.Description, and Drawer.Close don't get a vaul-branded
attribute, only Content and Handle do.

Props that existed to fight the page (scroll-lock, portal containers, manual keyboard handling,
fixed) are unnecessary here and warn once in dev. So do the Radix Dialog.Content-only props
Drawer.Content has no equivalent for (onPointerDownOutside, onOpenAutoFocus, onEscapeKeyDown,
onCloseAutoFocus, onInteractOutside, onFocusOutside, forceMount), stripped before they reach
the DOM rather than leaking through as unknown-prop warnings. Drawer.Overlay renders nothing
since the backdrop is automatic.

One accuracy divergence, deliberate: onRelease's second argument is the real open/closed
outcome here, true only when the sheet is staying open. Real vaul always passes true when
snapPoints is set, even on a release that dismisses the drawer.

Lifecycle callbacks: onAnimationEnd(open) fires once the transition visually finishes (the native
prop is onOpenChangeComplete), and onClose fires on every dismiss path, layered on onOpenChange.
Scrollsheet-native props with no vaul counterpart (backdropDismissible, escapeDismissible,
keyboardExpands, onTravel, scrollbar, actionsRef, animationSpeed) forward through Drawer.Root
untranslated.

## Migrate from Radix Dialog

    - import * as Dialog from '@radix-ui/react-dialog';
    + import { Dialog } from 'scrollsheet';

Dialog.Root, Trigger, Portal, Overlay, Content, Title, Description, and Close all exist and
render the centered presentation (a real <dialog> in the top layer, zoom+fade on a spring).
Root takes open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange, and modal, plus actionsRef, animationSpeed,
backdropDismissible, escapeDismissible, and onOpenChangeComplete. Content stamps
data-state="open" | "closed" so existing animation CSS keeps matching. Radix-only props
(onPointerDownOutside, onInteractOutside, onEscapeKeyDown, onOpenAutoFocus, onCloseAutoFocus,
onFocusOutside, forceMount, Portal container) are stripped and warn once in dev;
onPointerDownOutside and onInteractOutside map to backdropDismissible={false}, and
onEscapeKeyDown maps to escapeDismissible={false}. Dismissal fires on backdrop click, not
pointerdown. Overlay renders nothing; restyle the real backdrop with --scrollsheet-backdrop.

## Migrate from Sonner

    - import { toast, Toaster } from 'sonner';
    + import { toast, Toaster } from 'scrollsheet';

scrollsheet's Sonner compat layer is a drop-in: the same toast, useSonner, and Toaster
exports, running on the same architecture real Sonner uses: a persistent card per toast, all
portaled through one shared <section> in document.body, positioned with CSS instead of stacked
inside a shared sheet panel. toast(), .success(), .error(), .info(), .warning(), .loading(),
.message(), .custom(jsx), .promise(), and .dismiss(id?) all work before or after any <Toaster>
mounts, backed by the same module-level queue Sonner itself uses. A repeated id updates a toast
in place instead of pushing a second one, and multiple <Toaster id="..."> instances (toasterId is the deprecated prop name) route
independently: a toast() call with a matching toasterId only shows on that instance, everything
else on the default, un-keyed one.

All six Sonner positions render, and a toast's own position overrides the Toaster's default for
just that one toast. Every toast is a real, persistent card, not a ghost placeholder; collapsed
ones sit behind the front one and expand to the full list on hover or Alt+T (configurable via
hotkey). Escape dismisses the front toast, or collapses the stack back if the hotkey opened it,
though a stack the pointer is still hovering stays expanded until the pointer leaves. Swipe-to-dismiss tracks both axes: drag past 45px or flick it fast enough and it
dismisses, release short of that and it springs back. visibleToasts caps how many toasts show at
once, default 3; toasts past the cap stay mounted but hidden, timers still running, and fade in
the moment a slot frees, nothing gets evicted. Auto-dismiss uses each toast's own duration, or
the Toaster's, and pauses on hover, any pointer down on the stack (including mid-swipe),
keyboard expand, or a hidden tab.

Honest gaps, this being v1: theme stays the static light card; dark and system warn once rather
than silently no-op. richColors isn't implemented and warns once. toast.dismiss() with no id
clears every toast across every mounted <Toaster>, matching real Sonner's own dismiss() exactly.
useSonner() returns every toast across every toaster, unfiltered; a <Toaster id> does its
own filtering internally. A toast fired while a modal Sheet.Root is open renders behind it
rather than above it, matching real Sonner's own limitation against a native <dialog> elsewhere
on the page.

Sonner injects its styles automatically; scrollsheet's default entry expects two imports next to
the Toaster instead: scrollsheet/styles.css and scrollsheet/toast.css. For Sonner's zero-setup
behavior, import toast and Toaster from scrollsheet/auto instead: same components with the
stylesheet embedded, injected on first render.

## Browser support

| Browser | Spring easing | Compositor-driven backdrop dim + --scrollsheet-progress |
|---|---|---|
| Chrome / Edge | 113+ | 115+ |
| Safari | 17.2+ | 26+ |
| Firefox | 112+ | behind a flag, see below |

Safari 16.4 to 17.1 parses <dialog> but not CSS linear(), so the spring falls back to a plain
ease-out at the same duration. Below Safari 15.4 there is no <dialog> at all, so the sheet falls
back to a plain fixed-position modal (backdrop, tap-to-close, Escape, no detents or drag;
isSupported() reports which path a browser takes). scrollend falls back to a ~120ms debounced scroll-silence check where unsupported.

The backdrop dim and --scrollsheet-progress run as CSS scroll-driven animations
(animation-timeline: scroll()) on engines that support them, off the main thread entirely,
feature-detected once and stamped data-scrollsheet-sda on the dialog. Firefox has
animation-timeline: scroll() implemented but still ships it behind a flag as of mid-2026, and
Safari 17.2 through 25 has the spring but not scroll-driven animations yet; on both, and on
every engine below the compositor floor, the same numbers still update every frame from
onTravel's own JS write instead, same values, main thread rather than the compositor. Two
pieces stay JS-driven on every engine regardless: a stacked sheet's parent-panel recede (the
parent panel lives in a sibling top-layer <dialog>, not a descendant the track's timeline can
reach) and backgroundEffect (its target is an arbitrary page element outside the dialog
entirely).

Where dialog.closedBy exists (Chrome/Edge 134+, Firefox 141+), a modal sheet sets closedby to
closerequest when escapeDismissible is on, none when it's off, so Esc and the Android back
gesture route through the platform's own close-request machinery instead of scrollsheet's manual
handling. Never closedby="any": .scrollsheet-dialog always covers the full viewport, so there is
no "outside the dialog" region for a native light-dismiss to detect, and layering one on top of
the library's own backdrop-click handling would only risk a double-fire for no gain. Engines
without closedBy (Safari, as of this writing) keep the existing manual Esc/backdrop dismissal,
unchanged. Non-modal sheets (modal={false}) don't get a platform close watcher for free the way a
modal showModal() dialog does, so a dismissible one creates its own via CloseWatcher (Chrome
126+, Firefox 149+) so Android back closes it instead of navigating the page. Touch-primary devices only: Esc
is also a platform close signal wherever CloseWatcher exists, and non-modal Esc is deliberately
scoped to focus inside the sheet, so a desktop watcher would steal the page's Esc. Real-device
verification on that path is still pending.

## API

Full reference with every default: https://scrollsheet.dev/docs/reference/api

### Sheet.Root

| Prop | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| open | boolean | controlled |
| defaultOpen | boolean | false |
| onOpenChange | (open: boolean) => void | |
| onOpenChangeComplete | (open: boolean) => void | fires when the transition visually finishes |
| actionsRef | React.Ref<SheetActions> | open() / close() / snapTo(detent) |
| detents | readonly DetentSpec[] | ['content'] |
| activeDetent | DetentSpec | controlled |
| onActiveDetentChange | (detent: DetentSpec) => void | |
| sequentialDetents | boolean | false |
| dismissible | boolean | true |
| escapeDismissible | boolean | dismissible |
| backdropDismissible | boolean | dismissible |
| closeThreshold | number (0-1) | 0.5 |
| side | 'bottom' \| 'top' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'center' | 'bottom' |
| desktopSide | 'bottom' \| 'top' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'center' | unset: side applies at every width |
| desktopBreakpoint | number | 768 |
| modal | boolean | true |
| backgroundEffect | 'scale' \| 'parallax' \| 'none' | 'scale' for a full-height mobile bottom sheet opened from inside the marked wrapper, else off |
| backgroundRef | React.RefObject<HTMLElement \| null> | targets backgroundEffect directly |
| scrollbar | 'overlay' \| 'hidden' \| 'native' | 'overlay' |
| largestUndimmedDetent | DetentSpec | dims across the full range |
| handleOnly | boolean | false |
| disableDrag | boolean | false |
| onTravel | (revealedPx: number, progress: number, info: TravelInfo) => void | |
| onRelease | (event: PointerEvent, willRemainOpen: boolean) => void | |
| keyboardExpands | boolean | false |
| phantomScrollGuard | boolean | true |
| animationSpeed | number | 1 |
| nonce | string | |
| themeColorDimming | boolean | false |

### Sheet.Content, Sheet.Handle

| Prop | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Content fill | boolean | false |
| Content asChild | boolean | false |
| Handle variant | 'inside' \| 'floating' \| 'outside' | 'inside' |
| Handle asChild | boolean | false |

### Sheet.Content styling hooks

| Attribute / property | Where | Values |
|---|---|---|
| data-scrollsheet-state | <dialog> | pre \| opening \| open \| closing |
| data-scrollsheet-side | <dialog> | bottom \| top \| left \| right \| center |
| data-scrollsheet-modal | <dialog> | "false" when modal={false}, absent otherwise |
| data-scrollsheet-scrollbar | <dialog> | overlay \| hidden \| native |
| data-scrollsheet-at-max | <dialog> | present at tallest detent |
| data-scrollsheet-behind | <dialog> | present while a child sheet is open |
| data-scrollsheet-dragging | <dialog> | present during a desktop drag |
| data-scrollsheet-handle-only | <dialog> | present when handleOnly |
| data-scrollsheet-disable-drag | <dialog> | present when disableDrag |
| data-scrollsheet-detached | <dialog> | present once --scrollsheet-inset-bottom is set (the inset-card recipe) |
| data-scrollsheet-sda | <dialog> | present once CSS scroll-driven animations own the backdrop dim |
| data-scrollsheet-has-handle | <dialog> | present while a Sheet.Handle is rendered |
| data-scrollsheet-rtl | <dialog> | present when the panel's computed direction is rtl |
| data-scrollsheet-fill | panel and body | present when fill |
| data-scrollsheet-no-drag | anywhere | opts an element out of desktop drag |
| data-scrollsheet-backdrop | backdrop element | present on the built-in backdrop, for restyling it |
| data-scrollsheet-background | your page wrapper | marks the backgroundEffect target |
| data-scrollsheet-nested-scroll | an inner scroller | scrolls first, then hands off to sheet travel |
| data-scrollsheet-theme | an ancestor | dark \| system, anything else renders light |
| --scrollsheet-progress | backdrop element | 0 to 1, same value as onTravel. Set on the backdrop, not the dialog, so read it there (siblings don't inherit) |
| --scrollsheet-stack-progress | parent panel | 0 to 1, set while a child sheet is open |
| --scrollsheet-max-detent | <dialog> | tallest resolved detent, px |
| --scrollsheet-keyboard | <dialog> | on-screen-keyboard inset, px |
| --scrollsheet-backdrop | panel (set by you) | any CSS color |
| --scrollsheet-handle / -handle-hover | panel (set by you) | handle pill color, resting / hover |
| --scrollsheet-safe-area | panel (set by you) | usually env(safe-area-inset-bottom); -top, -left, -right exist too |
| --scrollsheet-radius | panel (set by you) | corner radius, default 16px |
| --scrollsheet-bg / --scrollsheet-fg | panel (set by you) | panel background / text color |
| --scrollsheet-shadow | panel (set by you) | panel box-shadow |
| --scrollsheet-close-bg / -close-bg-hover / -close-color / -close-color-hover | panel (set by you) | the self-closing <Sheet.Close /> button |
| --scrollsheet-inset-x / -top / -bottom / -left / -right / -y | panel (set by you) | px offsets for the "inset card" recipe |
| --scrollsheet-scrollbar-width / -color | panel (set by you) | overlay scrollbar thumb, default 4px; also styles nested-scroller thumbs |
| --scrollsheet-focus-ring / -width | handle (set by you) | keyboard focus ring on Sheet.Handle |
| --scrollsheet-travel | panel (set by you) | none turns off enter and exit travel |
| --scrollsheet-max-inline / -desktop-margin | panel (set by you) | docked desktop column width cap (640px) and edge margin (24px) |
| --scrollsheet-center-max-inline / -center-max-block / -center-gutter | panel (set by you) | side="center" guards: min(560px, 100%), 100%, 20px |

### Other exports

| Export | Extends / type |
|---|---|
| Sheet | namespace object: Root, Trigger, Content, Handle, Title, Description, Close |
| Sheet.Trigger | <button>, opens on click. asChild renders your own element instead |
| Sheet.Handle | <button>, drag grip; arrows/Home/End move detents, announces as a slider with 2+ detents. List detents shortest first. asChild supported |
| Sheet.Title / Sheet.Description | <h2> / <p>, auto-wires aria-labelledby / aria-describedby. asChild supported |
| Sheet.Close | <button>, closes on click. asChild supported. With no children it renders a styled X button |
| DetentSpec | 'full' \| 'medium' \| 'content' \| number \| `${number}px` |
| Side | 'bottom' \| 'top' \| 'left' \| 'right' (side and desktopSide also accept 'center') |
| SheetActions | { open(): void; close(): void; snapTo(detent: DetentSpec): void } |
| TravelInfo | { range: readonly [number, number]; progressAtDetents: ReadonlyMap<number, number> } |
| spring(config?) | { stiffness, damping, mass, velocity, restDelta } -> { easing, durationMs } (defaults 260, 30, 1, 0, 0.001) |
| isSupported() | () => boolean, false on the ~3% of browsers with no <dialog> |
| injectStylesInto(root, nonce?) / injectToastStylesInto(root, nonce?) | adopt the core / toast stylesheet into a shadow root; scrollsheet/auto only |
| Drawer | vaul-compatible namespace: Root, NestedRoot, Trigger, Portal, Overlay, Content, Handle, Title, Description, Close |
| Dialog | Radix-compatible namespace (centered presentation): Root, Trigger, Portal, Overlay, Content, Title, Description, Close |
| Toaster, toast, useToasts, useSonner | per-toast-DOM toasts; toast.success/error/info/warning/loading/message/custom/promise/dismiss/getToasts/getHistory |

### scrollsheet/motion (experimental)

spring, sampleSpringAt, animate, animateScrollTo, geometryFor, mapScroll, recedeTransform, and the
types SpringConfig, SpringCurve, AnimateHandle, ScrollAnimation, Side, SideGeometry. No semver
promise yet.
